currentContext.expansion: The Company's principal expansion is a new manufacturing facility at Howrah, West Bengal, funded substantially from the net proceeds of its BSE SME IPO. The MD&A states the facility is 'intended to expand installed capacity and setup capacity for Thermoforming and Paper Cup products' - the two product lines newly introduced alongside the existing thin-wall food containers, PLA straws and paper straws. The project was at an early stage at the FY26 balance-sheet date: MD&A prose notes capital work-in-progress rose sharply from Rs. 53.80 Lakhs to Rs. 1,188.85 Lakhs, 'consistent with initial site and foundation work at the new facility', with Rs. 3,219.47 Lakhs of issue proceeds placed in fixed deposits pending deployment toward the facility. Under the 'Expand Technological Capabilities' limb of its Strategic Growth Roadmap, management states it will 'Invest Rs. 10,022.00 lakhs in new manufacturing facilities and new production lines' and 'Enhance automation, drive operational efficiency, and cost competitiveness'. The new facility, together with product diversification into paper cups and thermoforming, is the stated underpinning of the ambition to reach roughly Rs. 50,000 Lakhs of turnover by FY29. Management explicitly flags execution risk: 'delay in commissioning the new manufacturing facility could defer expected growth and impair return on the associated capital expenditure.' No commissioning date, ramp schedule or capacity quantum for the project is disclosed in this bundle.

risks.note: MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' states a large share of revenue is derived from international customers, exposing the Company to trade-policy, tariff and geopolitical risk. Management separately attributes part of the FY26 pressure on growth momentum to prevailing geopolitical conflicts impacting export markets, so this is a live rather than theoretical exposure.

risks.risk: Input cost volatility - polymer / crude-linked raw materials
risks.note: MD&A flags that key raw materials are polymer/crude-linked and prices can be volatile. This bit in FY26: cost of materials consumed rose to roughly 62% of revenue from about 57%, attributed to an increase in crude oil prices, compressing the EBITDA margin from 24% to 19%.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the new Howrah manufacturing facility
risks.note: MD&A states that a delay in commissioning the new manufacturing facility could defer expected growth and impair return on the associated capital expenditure. The project carries the IPO proceeds and underpins the FY29 turnover ambition, so slippage hits both growth and returns.

MD&A flags regulatory risk from the shifting emphasis onto sustainable and environment-friendly packaging solutions - relevant to a business whose largest revenue line is thin-wall plastic food containers, even though PLA and paper straws sit on the other side of the same shift.

risks.risk: Working-capital intensity and the adequacy of inventory / receivables controls
risks.note: MD&A's internal-controls section states that, given the working-capital intensity of the business, the adequacy of inventory and receivables monitoring controls is particularly relevant to an assessment of financial risk - the company's own framing of where its financial risk concentrates.

risks.risk: Divergence between bank stock statements and the books of account
risks.note: The CARO annexure records that the Company has working-capital limits in excess of Rs. 5 crores secured on current assets, and that the March 2026 stock statement filed with banks was prepared before the financial-statement closure, 'which led to the differences between books of accounts and stock statement submitted with banks', covering inventory, trade receivables and trade payables.

The Rule 11 disclosure in the Joint Auditors' Report states the Company has two pending litigations with the GST Department, on which stay petitions were filed and stay has been granted by the Hon'ble Court. No amounts are disclosed in the routed text.
